manifest.name: dsh-plugin-settings-float
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: turn the settings dialog into a draggable, edge-resizable floating window that leaves the chat visible.

scripts.check: node --check lib/index.js && node --check lib/client.js && node --test test/*.test.mjs

bundle.text:
# dsh-plugin-settings-float bundle patch: one client-only row that lifts the
# settings dialog out of its centered overlay into a draggable floating panel.
- insert:
    - id: settings-float
      name: 'dsh-plugin-settings-float'

readme.text:
DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns the settings dialog into a **draggable, edge-resizable floating window**, so you can keep the chat visible (and usable) while changing settings.

The native settings surface is a centered modal with a full-screen scrim: it covers the conversation and cannot be moved. This plugin keeps the same React tree but lifts the panel out of the modal — no scrim, a floating panel you can drag by its header and resize from any edge or corner.

> ⚠️ This is a **DOM-level enhancement** built against the current DSH settings shell. The upstream bundle is never modified, and if a DSH upgrade changes the settings markup the plugin simply stops applying (the settings page keeps working as the native modal). Treat it as a convenience layer, not a fork.

- **Draggable** — grab the nav title or content header and move the window anywhere.
- **Eight resize handles** — drag any edge (↑↓←→) or corner (⤡ ⤢); opposite edges stay anchored.
- **Chat stays alive** — the dark scrim is removed and the overlay stops swallowing pointer events, so the conversation is visible and clickable behind the window.
- **Remembers geometry** — position and size persist in `localStorage` per browser profile.
- **Reset shortcuts** — double-click a header to snap back to the default spot; double-click a resize handle to restore the default size.
- **Configurable** — defaults, minimum size, enable switch and optional click-outside-to-close are exposed as a DSH plugin config card.

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Drag nav title / content header | Move the window |
| Drag any edge or corner | Resize (min size applies, viewport-clamped) |
| Double-click a header | Reset position to the default spot (right side, vertically centered) |
| Double-click a resize handle | Reset size to the configured default |
| Esc / ✕ | Close settings (unchanged) |

Open **Settings → Plugins → Settings Float** (the card is generated from the plugin schema), or set the row config in the profile patch:

```yaml
- id: settings-float
  name: dsh-plugin-settings-float
  config:
    enabled: true

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` keeps the native centered modal |
| `defaultWidth` / `defaultHeight` | `760` / `720` | Initial size, used until the user resizes once |
| `minWidth` / `minHeight` | `480` / `320` | Smallest size the window can be dragged to |
| `closeOnOutsideClick` | `false` | Sends `Escape` when the chat behind the window is clicked |

- Verified against DSH `0.2.1-rc.3` (desktop and web profile share the same settings shell).
- The panel is found by `role="dialog"` + settings-only children, with the release's hashed class only as a fast path — so a rename usually degrades gracefully instead of breaking.
- Requires a web-capable DSH surface (`dsh.client` platform `web`).

- No network requests, no host-side changes, no telemetry.
- Only two `localStorage` keys are written: `dsh.settings-float.pos.v1` and `dsh.settings-float.size.v1`.

```sh
npm install
npm test        # jsdom smoke tests: mount, 8-direction resize, drag, reset, config
```

Layout:

```
lib/index.js     host row: plugin entry + Config schema (the settings card)
lib/client.js    browser half: DOM enhancement, drag & resize
test/            jsdom smoke tests driving real pointer events
```

The client bundle uses DSH's client-module ABI (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`); `id` must match the package name.
